_meta.about: Places whose boundaries touch, for the free watchlist area (a place plus its neighbors). Keys and values are site place ids (<ST>:<Name>); keys starting with '_' are not places.
_meta.source: US Census Bureau, cartographic boundary files, 1:500,000: county subdivisions (MA, RI, NY, MI, OH), counties (VA, MD, MI, OH) and incorporated places (VA, MD)

method.rule: neighbors when the boundaries come within buffer_m of each other along at least min_shared_m; places across water the Census clips at the shoreline (ocean, sounds, Narragansett Bay, the Great Lakes) are not neighbors; across rivers and unclipped bays the line in the water counts
method.counties: Virginia and Maryland: a county's area is the touching counties and independent cities plus the towns inside it; a town's area is its county (both when it straddles a line) plus the towns and cities it touches. Michigan and Ohio: townships, cities and villages touch; each includes its county; counties touch; a regional planning body covers its counties' places
method.projection: equirectangular at latitude 42.5 (MA, RI, NY), 38.2 (VA, MD), 42.5 (MI, OH)
method.names: places on the site keep their site id; other NY names used by more than one town or city get ' (city)' or ' (<County> County)' added; Michigan and Ohio townships are '<Name> Township' or '<Name> Charter Township', a repeated name with ' (<County> County)'; cities are 'City of <Name>', villages 'Village of <Name>'; Virginia and Maryland towns 'Town of <Name>', cities 'City of <Name>' (Baltimore City keeps its name); New York City's boroughs are listed by name; a city split across counties is one entry; NY Indian reservations are left out
method.states: MA, RI, NY, VA, MD, MI and OH, including neighbors across the MA, RI and NY lines and the VA and MD line; other states are not included
